summary: Checked all changed doc blocks (trait ExprMap summary; transformChildren incl. its Closure @note; transformStatement, transformDefinition, transformTermChildren, transformTerm, transformTypeTree, transformCaseDef, transformTypeCaseDef, transformStats, transformDefinitions, both transformTerms overloads incl. the @throws MatchError, transformTypeTrees, transformCaseDefs, transformTypeCaseDefs) against the implementation, including the underlying dotc TreeCopier/cpy eq-check behavior (Trees.scala) that justifies the 'returned unchanged when nothing changed' and 'tree itself is returned' claims, and the Closure/Lambda encoding in Quotes.scala that justifies the bare-Closure @note. All descriptions, @param, @return and the one @throws tag accurately match the code; only two minor wording nits found, no blockers.

items.issue: The @return uses present-perfect phrasing ('have been replaced') rather than the simple present tense used elsewhere in the file's tags.
items.suggestion: Reword to 'are replaced by the result of applying transform to them' for tense consistency.

items.issue: The repeated tag '@param owner the symbol that owns tree' applies to all 4 occurrences (lines 42, 90, 167, 200). It is not false, but it's an informal shorthand: none of Statement/Term/CaseDef actually have their own 'owner' in the symbol-table sense — 'owner' is really the ambient enclosing-scope symbol threaded through the traversal for use when new symbols/trees are constructed, not literally 'the symbol that owns tree'.
items.suggestion: Optionally reword to something like 'the current owner symbol in whose scope tree is transformed' for precision; not required since the existing phrasing is a defensible, consistently-used convention.
